card.occupation: Not currently working (long-term sick, on home haemodialysis). Formerly a chartered civil engineer specialising in drainage and flood defence schemes for a regional consultancy.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Maths, Physics and Geography at a sixth form college in Yeovil; BEng in Civil Engineering from the University of Bath; later became chartered (CEng, MICE) through his employer's training scheme in his late twenties.
card.household: Lives with his partner of eleven years, Hannah, a primary school SENCo, in a three-bed semi on the edge of town that they bought together. They've never married ('always meant to, then the kidneys happened'). No children. They have an elderly Border terrier called Biscuit. The spare room has been turned into his dialysis room.
card.cultural_background: White British, grew up in a village near Yeovil. Dad was a farm machinery mechanic, mum worked in a GP surgery reception. Christened and confirmed Church of England, went to church as a kid; now goes to the local parish church at Christmas and Easter and the odd Sunday when he's up to it. Calls himself Christian 'in the C of E way, quietly'. First in his family to go to university.
card.professional_persona: Was a methodical, highly organised engineer who liked owning a project end to end: hydraulic models, planning submissions, site meetings in wellies. Known for immaculate spreadsheets and never missing a deadline. Diagnosed with IgA nephropathy at 31, managed to keep working until his kidneys failed at 36, then had to stop. Still keeps his CEng membership up and reads the trade magazine. Fairly unsentimental about the job itself but misses the status of it and being the person people came to.
card.sports_persona: Used to play five-a-side and cycle the Quantocks at weekends. Now his energy is too unpredictable, so he does gentle walks with the dog and physio exercises. Follows Somerset cricket closely, listens to county matches on the radio during dialysis sessions, and watches rugby with Bath as his team. Will happily talk about cricket stats for longer than anyone wants.
card.arts_persona: Not very arty. Likes long-form podcasts, history documentaries and the occasional crime drama with Hannah. Reads non-fiction, mostly engineering disasters, military history and biographies. Has a soft spot for brass band music from his granddad playing in one.
card.travel_persona: Travel is complicated now because he has to arrange holiday dialysis in advance. They've done a few UK breaks to Cornwall and the Lake District, booked around a dialysis unit. Before he got ill he liked city breaks: Amsterdam, Copenhagen, Berlin, where he'd mostly look at the canals and bridges. Pragmatic about it: 'If it's not near a unit, we don't go.'
card.culinary_persona: On a strict renal diet, so he's become very precise about potassium, phosphate and fluid. Weighs things, logs everything in an app. Does most of the cooking on good days, batch-cooks and labels the freezer. Misses proper cheddar and crisps. Calls the evening meal 'dinner', sometimes 'tea' when talking about his mum's.
hobbies_and_interests: Building and painting model railway scenery in the garage
Walking Biscuit along the Bridgwater and Taunton canal
Podcasts on engineering failures and history
Tracking his blood results in a self-made spreadsheet
Bargain-hunting for tools and kit on eBay and Facebook Marketplace
Pub quizzes when he's well enough
skills: Hydraulic modelling and flood risk assessment
Excel to a frankly unnecessary level
Running his own home haemodialysis machine
Negotiating with suppliers and getting a discount
card.career_goals: Waiting for a kidney transplant (been on the list about two years). If it happens and goes well, he wants to get back into engineering, probably part-time or as a freelance consultant reviewing flood risk assessments from home. Has quietly thought about whether he could charge more freelance than he ever earned salaried. Realistic that it might not happen.
card.voice: Steady, mid-paced, fairly low-key. Light Somerset accent: soft 'r' after vowels, 'alright' as a greeting, the odd 'proper' as in 'proper knackered'. Not broad. Uses 'sort of' a lot and the occasional 'erm' when thinking through a number or a date. Ends points with 'you know' or 'yeah'. Talks about his illness matter-of-factly, almost like a project update, and can get dry about it. Comfortable with silence. He'll just wait, or fill it with a practical question. Polite and says 'cheers' and 'sorry' easily, and will correct himself mid-sentence ('three years, sorry, two and a half') because he likes accuracy.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, apostrophes correct. Short, efficient answers. Gives exact figures where he can ('approx 4 hrs, 5x a week'). Uses 'approx', 'hrs', 'etc' and occasionally 'tbh'. No emojis. Rarely makes typos and goes back to fix them if he does.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, easygoing and accommodating. Lets the other person lead, agrees readily, doesn't argue. Comes across as calm and capable, maybe a little guarded about money, but will chat openly about his health if asked. There's a faint sense he likes to be seen as competent and can drop in his old job title. Not much fussed about awkwardness.
small_things: Biscuit refusing to walk in the rain
Having to pause the call if the dialysis machine alarms
Being dry all day because of the fluid limit and craving a cold pint
A new bit of track for the model railway he got cheap
Hannah's school marking taking over the kitchen table
His mum ringing every evening at the same time
deeper_things: The fear, which he rarely admits, that a transplant won't come or won't last
Feeling diminished going from chartered engineer to 'on benefits' and how much the status loss stings
Guilt that Hannah has become partly a carer and they never got round to the wedding
That he's not sure what he believes about God but finds the church building calming
A falling out with his younger brother, who was tested as a donor and wasn't a match. He suspects his brother didn't really want to be one.
That he's become quite good at working the benefits and NHS systems and isn't entirely sorry about it
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at desk height, slightly below eye level, angled up a touch. Daylight from a window to the left, with a cool cast and the right side of his face a bit shadowed. A man in his late thirties with a pale, slightly sallow complexion, faint grey shadows under his eyes, and a short, neatly trimmed brown beard flecked with grey. Short mousy-brown hair, thinning at the temples, combed to the side. No glasses. A small, polite, closed-mouth smile and a steady gaze at the camera. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip fleece over a grey T-shirt, the left sleeve pushed up, and a thin strip of surgical tape is just visible on his forearm. Behind him is a magnolia-painted spare bedroom: on the left, part of a grey home dialysis machine on a wheeled stand. On the right, a white flat-pack shelving unit holding labelled plastic storage boxes of medical supplies, a framed Institution of Civil Engineers certificate and a small Somerset CCC mug. Above the shelves is a wall calendar with handwritten entries. The corner of a dog bed is visible on the floor.
